en: Now begins the hymn of twelve names dedicated to Dattātreya. Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Of this mantra, the hymn of the twelve names of the illustrious Dattātreya:
the Paramahaṃsa is the seer (ṛṣi);
the supreme self, the illustrious Dattātreya, is the deity (devatā).
The meter is Anuṣṭubh.
The application is for the purpose of accomplishing all desires during recitation.
The first is indeed the Great Yogin.
The second was Prabhurīśvara;
the third was Trimūrti;
and the fourth was Jñānasāgara.
The fifth is Jñānavijñāna;
the sixth is Sarvamaṅgala;
the seventh is Puṇḍarīkākṣa.
The eighth is Devavallabha;
the ninth is Nandadeveśa;
the tenth is Nandadāyaka.
The eleventh is Mahārudra;
the twelfth is Karuṇākara.
These are the twelve names of the great-souled Dattātreya.
Renowned as the King of Mantras, this supreme [mantra] of Dattātreya and Hara wards off consumption,
epilepsy, leprosy, and other ailments, as well as the fever of affliction.
It is effective at the royal court, on the road, in fearsome battles, and amidst the waters.
Whether in the interior of a house, in the forest, or amidst fears of tigers and thieves,
those who recite this during thousands of rebirths obtain their desired fruit.
He who recites it constantly at the three times of day shall attain the perfection of liberation.

O Dattātreya, he shall always protect his fame and truth; of this there is no doubt. The seeker of knowledge obtains knowledge, the sick man is liberated from disease, the childless man obtains a son, and the poor man obtains wealth.
One without a wife obtains a wife; one seeking happiness obtains happiness;
he is liberated from all sins and becomes victorious everywhere.
Thus ends the hymn of praise consisting of the twelve names of the illustrious Dattātreya.
May this be offered unto Śrī Dattātreya.
